Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to open the innings for India. Lea Tahuhu will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for New Zealand. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand have the momentum heading into the second half, especially after forging a recovery from a dire position of 88/5. They will be eager to strike early and put India on the back foot, just as they've done in the last couple of games. As for India, the openers need to step up in this decider and provide a solid start - something they’ve struggled with throughout the series. It’s all set up for an intriguing chase. We will be back shortly for India’s response!

Priya Mishra is in for a chat. She says that she is very happy that her dream of playing for India has come true. Adds that she did the celebration without thinking of anything specific and it is normal for her. Mentions that Harmanpreet told her that Devine was being troubled by the googlies, so she bowled only that to her. Ends by saying that she was very nervous at the start but once she bowled the first ball everything was under control.

Both batters took a measured approach, navigating the Indian spin threat with care. Gaze contributed 25 before her dismissal, after which Halliday sensed the need for urgency and injected some impetus into the innings. Battling through the heat, she managed to find the boundaries and kept fighting to lift New Zealand's total. 76 runs came off the last 10 overs and India will feel that they let New Zealand get away after having them on the ropes at one stage.

Just as the White Ferns were beginning to build momentum, Bates was dismissed via a run-out, quickly followed by a couple more wickets, leaving New Zealand wobbling at 36/3 in the 11th over. India’s spinners tightened their grip in the middle phase, and just as partnerships began to form, timely breakthroughs, including the dismissals of Plimmer and Green, pegged the visitors back. At 88/5, Izzy Gaze joined Brooke Halliday in the 24th over with the crucial task of stabilizing the innings.

Well, it turned out to be a tale of two halves, with India dominating the first half and reducing New Zealand to 89/5 at the halfway mark. However, from that precarious position, New Zealand fought their way back into the game, showcasing resilience and determination. Although they may have had a different total in mind after opting to bat first, they can take some satisfaction in their recovery and the final score. Earlier in the game, India maintained discipline with both the ball and were sharp in the field from the outset.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the start of the decider! The India Women players are already in their respective field positions. Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer are the two openers for New Zealand Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - WV Raman is near the deck. He informs that pitch number 7 will be used for this game. It’s a surface composed entirely of red soil, which tends to provide extra bounce. He mentions that the straight boundary measures 69 meters, while the square boundaries are equidistant at 58 metres. Says that the pitch appears hard but slightly dry, which may bring spin into play as the game progresses. Raman concludes that the team with sharper shot selection could have the upper hand on this wicket.
JUST IN - We have news coming in from the Indian camp that Shreyanka Patil was unavailable for selection for this game due to shin splints.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, Lauren Down, Sophie Devine (C), Brooke Halliday, Maddy Green, Izzy Gaze (WK), Hannah Rowe (In for Jess Kerr), Lea Tahuhu, Eden Carson, Fran Jonas.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Yastika Bhatia (WK), Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Tejal Hasabnis, Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Saima Thakor, Priya Mishra, Renuka Singh Thakur (In for Arundhati Reddy).
TOSS - New Zealand Women have won the toss and they will BAT first.

After the disappointment of the World Cup, India will be eager to taste the success of a series win, while New Zealand seek a memorable overseas series win to boost their standing in the Women’s Championship. All in all, the setting is perfect for a thrilling finale, and with the series on the line, both teams are sure to deliver a match worth following. Stick around for the toss and team news.

New Zealand, on the other hand, have displayed their characteristic resilience, bouncing back in the second ODI to level the series. Sophie Devine’s brilliant all-round performance - where she led with both bat and ball and illustrated why she’s so highly regarded. Devine’s leadership and her sheer determination to win have been central to New Zealand’s success in this series. Suzie Bates has also brought in a wealth of experience at the top, anchoring the innings with her steady, calculated approach and guiding younger players along the way.

For India, their openers, particularly Smriti Mandhana, haven’t quite fired in this series. Today presents a perfect chance for her to step up and give India the strong foundation they need. Despite these early batting setbacks, their middle and lower-middle order has risen to the occasion with Tejal Hasabnis being the central figure. The emergence of Saima Thakor as a promising pacer has also added depth to India’s bowling arsenal, particularly in the absence of Pooja Vastrakar. Her discipline and ability to pick up timely wickets could play a pivotal role in today’s decider.

Hello and welcome everyone to the highly anticipated series decider between India Women and New Zealand Women! We’re here at the iconic Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, where both teams will battle it out one last time in this ODI series. With the series level at 1-1, we couldn’t ask for a better setting or higher stakes. Ahmedabad’s sweltering heat has been unrelenting, adding to the challenges faced by both sides, yet neither team has backed down, delivering cricket of the highest quality.
